title: The glued twisting sheaf O(1) of P^n_Z is the sheaf attached to S(1)
statement: Let $n$ be a finite nonempty index set, $S=\mathbf Z[T_k:k\in n]$ graded by total degree, $P=\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj] with standard opens $U_i=D_+(T_i)$, $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_P)=S_{(T_i)}$. Let $\mathcal O_P(1)$ be the invertible module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] (with $A=\mathbf Z$, $d=1$): glued from the free modules $\mathcal O_{U_i}e_i$ with $e_i=(T_i/T_j)\,e_j$ on $U_i\cap U_j$; for $k\in n$ let $T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k\in\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$ be the global section with $T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k|_{U_i}=(T_k/T_i)\,e_i$ for every $i$ (these agree on overlaps by the transition rule). Let $\widetilde{S(1)}$ be the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_P$-module attached to the shifted graded $S$-module $S(1)$, so $\widetilde{S(1)}(D_+(f))=(S_f)_1$ for homogeneous $f$ of positive degree, with the global sections $T_k$ given by $T_k/1\in(S_f)_1$ on every $D_+(f)$. Then there is exactly one isomorphism of $\mathcal O_P$-modules $\theta:\mathcal O_P(1)\to\widetilde{S(1)}$ with $\theta(e_i)=T_i/1\in(S_{T_i})_1$ for every $i$, and $\theta(T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k)=T_k$ for every $k$.

source.place: Constructions, Section 01MM (label section-invertible-on-proj) and Lemma 01MS (label lemma-when-invertible: O(d)|_{D_+(f)} is trivial with generator f for f of degree d); glueing of morphisms of sheaves: Sheaves, Section 00AK / Lemma 00AL (literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex)

proof.text: *Matching the objects with clause (v) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts].* Since $n$ is finite and nonempty, choose a bijection $n\cong\{0,\dots,N\}$ ($N=|n|-1\ge0$) and relabel the variables; nothing below depends on the labels. Then $S=\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_N]$, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ and $\widetilde{S(1)}$ with its global sections $T_k$ ($T_k/1\in(S_f)_1$ on every $D_+(f)$) are exactly the objects $\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}$, $\mathcal O(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] and $T_0,\dots,T_N$ of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts]. The glued $\mathcal O_P(1)$ of the present statement is the module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] with $A=\mathbf Z$, $x_k=T_k$, $d=1$, $e_i=e_i^{(1)}$, transition rule $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$: this is the module $\mathcal L$ of clause (v) with its bases $e_j$. The global section $T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k$ satisfies $T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k|_{U_j}=(T_k/T_j)e_j$ for every $j$, which is the defining property of the section $x_k$ of clause (v); as the $U_j$ cover $P$ (clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts]) a section of the sheaf $\mathcal L$ is determined by its restrictions to the $U_j$, so $T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k=x_k$. Finally the section $T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ of clause (v) is the element $T_j/1\in(S_{T_j})_1=\widetilde{S(1)}(U_j)$, by the description of the global sections $T_k$ (restriction to every $D_+(f)$ is $T_k/1$; [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]).

source.place: Lemma 01MS (label lemma-when-invertible, d = 1) and the glueing of morphisms of sheaves (Sheaves, Lemma 00AL), as carried out in step 7 (clause (v)) of lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By clause (v) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts] there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_P$-modules $\Phi:\mathcal L\to\widetilde{S(1)}$ with $\Phi(e_j)=T_j|_{U_j}$ for all $j$, and $\Phi(x_k)=T_k$ for all $k$. Translating by step 1 ($\mathcal L=\mathcal O_P(1)$, $T_j|_{U_j}=T_j/1$, $x_k=T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k$), $\theta:=\Phi$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_P(1)\to\widetilde{S(1)}$ with $\theta(e_i)=T_i/1$ for every $i$ and $\theta(T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k)=T_k$ for every $k$. Uniqueness: any isomorphism $\theta'$ with $\theta'(e_i)=T_i/1$ for all $i$ is a $\Phi'$ with $\Phi'(e_j)=T_j|_{U_j}$ for all $j$, hence $\theta'=\Phi=\theta$ by the uniqueness in clause (v). (Clause (v) is proved in step 7 of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts] exactly along Stacks 01MS and the glueing of morphisms: local isomorphisms $a\,e_j\mapsto a\,T_j|$, compatible on $U_i\cap U_j$ by $T_i|=(T_i/T_j)T_j|$, glued in the sheaf $\mathcal Hom$ [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-is-sheaf].)
